purpose: Insulin glargine-yfgn is used to help control blood sugar levels in adults and children with diabetes. It works over a full 24 hours to keep your blood sugar steady throughout the day and night. It is used for both type 1 and type 2 diabetes.
how_it_works: Your body normally makes insulin to help sugar from your food get into your cells for energy. If your body does not make enough insulin or cannot use it well, your blood sugar stays too high. This medicine acts like the insulin your body should be making, slowly releasing over 24 hours to keep your blood sugar at a safe level.
common_side_effects: The most common side effect is low blood sugar (hypoglycemia), which can make you feel shaky, sweaty, dizzy, or confused. You may also notice redness, swelling, or itching at the injection site. Some people gain a little weight while using insulin.
warnings: Low blood sugar is the most serious risk — always have a fast-acting sugar source (like juice or glucose tablets) nearby. Never share your insulin pen or needles with anyone else. Do not use this insulin in an IV or insulin pump. Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or are sick, since your dose may need to change. Avoid drinking too much alcohol, as it can affect your blood sugar.
typical_dosing: This insulin is given as a shot under the skin (subcutaneous injection) once a day, at the same time every day. Your doctor will set your starting dose and adjust it based on your blood sugar readings. Never change your dose on your own without talking to your doctor or pharmacist first.
